contentMap.abstract: This report describes a web-based academic project documentation system developed for final year students. The system is intended to keep university formatting rules consistent while the report content is written and revised.
contentMap.ack: The authors thank the department faculty and laboratory staff for guidance during the development of this project.
contentMap.ch1: This chapter introduces the project, its purpose, and the academic context in which the system is developed.
contentMap.ch1-1: The proposed system provides a structured workspace for preparing a final year project report according to university guidelines.
contentMap.ch1-2: The purpose of the system is to reduce manual formatting effort and keep chapter structure aligned with departmental requirements.
contentMap.ch1-3: Primary stakeholders include students, supervisors, and departmental reviewers who examine the completed report.
contentMap.ch1-4: The system is expected to improve consistency of submitted reports and reduce time spent on page setup and heading styles.
contentMap.ch1-5: Existing manual report preparation practices rely on local Word templates and repeated correction of formatting mistakes.
contentMap.ch2: This chapter records the functional and non-functional requirements identified for the system.
contentMap.ch2-1: Functional requirements describe the services that the system must provide to student and supervisor users.
contentMap.ch2-1-1: The authentication module controls access to project workspaces.
contentMap.ch2-1-1-1: Login policy defines how registered users gain access to the editor.
contentMap.ch2-1-1-1-1: Password rules require a minimum length and prevent reuse of the previous password.
contentMap.ch2-2: Non-functional requirements cover performance, security, and maintainability constraints.
contentMap.ch3: This chapter outlines the analysis and design of the proposed system.
contentMap.ch3-1: The system architecture separates the web editor from the document generation engine.
